heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles SainSmart Glow TPU reliably when routed from an external spool holder, reaching a safe maximum print speed of 48 mm/s based on its 4 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. However, printing this abrasive phosphorescent filament safely requires upgrading the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears to hardened steel components.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap the Max Volumetric Speed to 4.0 mm³/s in the Filament settings to prevent extruder slipping and under-extrusion.
Set Retraction Length to 0.8 mm and Retraction Speed to 30 mm/s to minimize TPU stringing without grinding the soft filament.
Bypass the Bambu AMS entirely by feeding directly from an external dry box or the rear spool holder to prevent catastrophic feed jams.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (1 mm) and set Seam Position to 'Aligned' or 'Rear' to mitigate flexible oozing artifacts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clogs and filament wraps around the drive gears
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Feeding flexible TPU through the AMS or pushing volumetric speeds beyond the safe 4 mm³/s threshold.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Feed the spool externally through the PTFE tube directly into the toolhead and set Max Volumetric Speed to 4.0 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rapid nozzle wear and loss of dimensional accuracy
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive strontium aluminate glow particles eroding the stock P1S stainless steel nozzle orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an official Bambu Lab 0.4mm or 0.6mm hardened steel complete hotend assembly before printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing, rough surface texture, and popping sounds during extrusion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High moisture absorption by the TPU polymer during ambient exposure.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 55°C for at least 8 hours in an active filament dryer and print directly from a sealed enclosure.

faq.question: Can I feed SainSmart Glow TPU through the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: No, TPU is too flexible for the AMS internal rollers and long PTFE guide paths, leading to severe binding and gear jams; always use the external spool holder.

faq.question: Why is a hardened steel nozzle required for glow-in-the-dark TPU?
faq.answer: Glow TPU contains phosphorescent ceramic particles (typically strontium aluminate) that rapidly grind down stock stainless steel nozzles, enlarging the aperture within a single spool.

faq.question: Should I print Glow TPU with the P1S door open or closed?
faq.answer: Printing with the front door cracked open or the top glass vented is recommended to maintain a low chamber temperature and prevent flexible TPU heat creep.

faq.question: Why is glue stick necessary on the Textured PEI Plate for TPU?
faq.answer: TPU bonds excessively well to clean PEI, which can cause permanent damage or tear the PEI coating off the plate upon removal; the glue stick acts as a sacrificial release agent.
